races.title: State Assembly, District 16
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Rebecca Bauer-Kahan
cands.bio: Democrat and attorney who has represented Assembly District 16 (Lamorinda to the Tri-Valley) since 2018. Former environmental and immigration attorney and law professor at Santa Clara University and Golden Gate University. Chairs the Assembly Privacy and Consumer Protection Committee.

endorsements.text: Democratic Party of California (2026 endorsement listed by Ballotpedia)
California Federation of Labor Unions, AFL-CIO (2026)
SEIU Local 521 and International Union of Operating Engineers Local 3 (2026)

cands.gaps: We found no documented stances or actions by Bauer-Kahan on data centers, homestead property tax elimination, limits on investor or foreign land buying, growth limits and land protection, H-1B or immigration enforcement, police pay and pensions, or school choice and teacher pay. She did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2020, 2022, 2024 or 2026, so we have no questionnaire answers from her. No controversies or foreign ties appeared in the pages we read. The pages we read give no information on her parents' backgrounds beyond her grandparents' arrival as refugees in 1939.

local.label: Roots 100: Wikipedia says she was born in Portola Valley, California, spent her childhood in the Bay Area and attended Bay Area public schools; she returned to the Bay Area in 2005 after practicing law in Washington, D.C.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Assembly member since 2018 (assistant speaker pro tempore for one term); earlier an environmental, intellectual-property and immigration attorney and a law professor at Santa Clara University (from 2010) and Golden Gate University (from 2014).
qual.why: Eight years of prior legislative service, a brief chamber leadership post and a law and policy career place her in the high band; committee chairmanships were not counted.
qual.label: Eight years of prior legislative service, a brief chamber leadership post and a law and policy career place her in the high band; committee chairmanships were not counted.

pro-life.evidence: Authored AB 2099, which increases penalties for harassing reproductive health patients and providers.

second-amendment.evidence: Authored AB 2047, the Firearm Printing Prevention Act, which requires 3D printers sold in California to include technology that blocks printing of firearms or machine-gun conversion devices once state standards are set.

prio.label: Matches 0 of 2 priorities; 2 backed by their record, 0 only promised

cands.name: Joseph A. Rubay
cands.bio: Republican from Contra Costa County. Real estate appraiser who owned and ran his own appraisal business for over 30 years. Chaired, and now vice-chairs, the Alamo Police Services Advisory Committee. Has run for California State Assembly District 16 several times, most recently in 2026. Has held no elected office.

endorsements.text: Republican Party of California (listed for 2026, and also for 2024)

cands.gaps: We found no record of what Rubay has done on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buyers, growth and land protection, H-1B or immigration enforcement, gun policy, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. His campaign site makes only general statements on taxes, housing costs and local control of zoning, which don't clearly address those topics. We could not find his birthplace, where he grew up, or when he came to California. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2020, 2022, 2024 or 2026. We found no news coverage or controversies about him.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.
score.why_money: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Owned and operated a real estate appraisal business for more than 30 years, with a degree in Accounting and Business Management from CSU East Bay. He has held no elected office. He has served on a county police advisory committee and the county fair board, and worked on political campaigns.
qual.why: Scored in the middle band for 30+ years as a business owner. Advisory committee and fair board seats add nothing, and he has no legislative service or policy or budget career.
qual.label: Scored in the middle band for 30+ years as a business owner. Advisory committee and fair board seats add nothing, and he has no legislative service or policy or budget career.

back-police-order.evidence: His campaign site says he would fully fund local law enforcement, oppose "defund the police" efforts, and end early-release policies for violent offenders.

prio.label: Matches 1 of 1 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 1 only promised (needs 2 to score)
